name: veterinary_clinic_system_062_transfer_approval_flow
instruction: Process the transfer queue the way the Locations → Transfers screen does. For every location_transfers row with status 'pending' whose note does NOT contain the word 'specialist' (case-insensitive), complete it: set status to 'completed', completed_at to the episode timestamp, update the patient's location_id to the transfer's to_location_id, and append one audit_log row {actor: 'Dana Whitaker', actor_role: 'org_admin', action: 'TRANSFER_COMPLETED', target_collection: 'patients', target_id: <patient id>, details: 'Transfer completed <batch_code>: loc <from> -> loc <to>.', occurred_at: episode timestamp}. Leave specialist-hold and already-approved transfers untouched. Then push one ops_reports row {report: 'transfer_sweep', batch_code, completed_now, specialist_holds, approved_untouched, completed_total} computed from the live queue, send one communications summary to owner id '1' with subject 'Transfer sweep <batch_code>' and body 'Processed <completed_now> routine transfer(s); <specialist_holds> specialist hold(s); <approved_untouched> pre-approved transfer(s); <completed_total> completed in total.', and make the whole sweep idempotent.
_par_steps_note: placeholder -- measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: placeholder -- set to roughly par_steps * 1.5 after live measurement

success_criteria.summary: The two seed pending non-specialist transfers are completed, have completed_at on the episode date, and the corresponding patients' location_id is rewritten to to_location_id. The specialist-hold and approved transfers and their patients remain untouched. There are exactly two new TRANSFER_COMPLETED audit rows, one ops_reports transfer_sweep row, and one communications summary. All counts are derived independently from the live state and the seed snapshot, with dual-path (Python and SQL) verification where applicable.

checks.expect: target transfers completed with patient moves; non-targets untouched; one report and one comm with live counts
status counts and completed_now agree between Python and SQL

hazards: specialist-hold decoy: transfer id 7 has status 'pending' and note 'Specialist follow-up at Riverside' (capital S); a case-insensitive 'specialist' check is required, otherwise patient 30 is incorrectly moved.

approved-transfer decoy: transfer id 4 has status 'approved' and empty note; a solution that processes all non-completed rows (or all rows without 'specialist' regardless of status) will move patient 19 and fail.
pre-existing completed transfers (ids 3, 5, 6) must remain exactly as seeded; the audit trail for this batch is independent and must not alter them.
idempotency: re-running must not create duplicate audit rows, duplicate communications, or duplicate ops_reports; the sweep keys its report/communication by batch.
patient location consistency: the patient's new location_id must equal the transfer's to_location_id, not from_location_id.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines a status + text-filter queue sweep, patient-location rewrite, audit trail, live-count report, and summary communication. The case-insensitive specialist exclusion and the approved-state decoy are classic front-desk logic that separate it from simple state-machine tasks.
